messages.author: 4fdc04b06b76c8cf
messages.subject: layout() in combination with ggplot2?
parts:
Hello,

I want to place two plots in one row with two different width.
These two plots don't share any axis so the usual facet approach
might not be the one I want.

With usual plots (plot()) I am able to do that with:

layout(matrix(c(1,2), 1, 2, byrow = TRUE),widths=c(2,1))

But when it doesn't work with these two plots:


ggplot(data, aes(x=Vs,y=Vm))+
geom_point()+
geom_text(aes(0.1,1000,label=cor.text))+
stat_smooth(method="lm",se=T,colour="black")+
theme_bw()

ggplot(data.Vs_Vm)+
geom_boxplot(aes(y=(Vm/Vs),x="box"))+
theme_bw()+
opts(axis.title.x=theme_blank(),
axis.text.x=theme_blank(),
panel.grid.major = theme_blank(),
panel.grid.minor = theme_blank())

where the first should be 2/3 of the width and the second 1/3.

Is there any other simple approach like layout() for ggplot2?

best regards

Johannes

messages.author: 4fdc04b06b76c8cf
messages.subject: Re: layout() in combination with ggplot2?
parts:
Thank you, that was a good hint. I did it now following way with 2 ggplots:

grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout = grid.layout(1, 2,widths=c(2.5,1))))
print(plot1, vp = viewport(layout.pos.row = 1, layout.pos.col = 1))
print(plot2, vp = viewport(layout.pos.row = 1, layout.pos.col = 2))

Is that somehow okay to do that? Or is there any other and better way?


There are just two more things I'd like to change:

1) My second plot doesn't have any x-axis because I set it with the opts:
opts(axis.title.x=theme_blank(),axis.text.x=theme_blank())
Now there is the problem that the two plots aren't aligned correctly. Is there any option where I can align the two plots according to the line of the x axis? Maybe instead of setting the axis theme_blank, just making the color of the text invisible?

2) Is it possible to change the y axis of the second plot to the right (instead of the default left side)? I read that it was planned to be implemented (http://r.789695.n4.nabble.com/How-to-change-the-default-location-of-x-axis-in-ggplot2-td3161204.html) but is that already done? Or is there any other way to just swap the axis to the right side instead of the left side?

Thank you

Johannes

messages.subject: Re: layout() in combination with ggplot2?
parts:
Johannes:
Baptiste knows more about this but here are my two $
My graphic background colour defaults to the cornsilk color so you might want
to change to white or whatever your default backround colour is.
library(gridExtra)
plot1 <- qplot(1:15,1:15)
plot2 <- qplot(1:5,1:5) +  opts(axis.title.x=theme_text(colour='cornsilk'),
axis.ticks=theme_segment(colour='cornsilk'),axis.text.x=theme_text(colour='cornsilk'))
grid.arrange(plot1,plot2,nrow=1,widths=c(2,1))
 
I am not sure about question # 2 and I don't think ggplot supports the Y axis on the right side(I could be wrong) :)
